item.title: HTML5 print mode emits "page 1" even without TOC

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use config `testing/myconfig_html5.json` with `html5.mode : "print"` and run: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Open `testing/lowlands-debug.html` and inspect generated CSS @page rules.
Observe `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` and visible page-number output (e.g. page 1), even when no TOC section is present.

item.expected-result: When TOC is not involved, page-number rendering should be controllable and not appear unexpectedly; users should be able to disable footer page numbers in HTML5 print mode without custom CSS surgery.

analysis.hypothesis: The output is generated in paged mode (`body.chordpro-paged`) because `html5.mode` is set to `print` in the active config. In paged mode, @page margin boxes are always generated from PDF format rules.

`lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5Helper/FormatGenerator.pm` translates `%{page}` to `counter(page)` for footer slots. The effective default PDF format includes a footer page marker, producing `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` in generated CSS.

The page number is not TOC-driven in this reproduction. TOC-specific selectors only suppress page numbers on `@page toc`, but no TOC block is required for default page footer counters to appear on song pages.
analysis.root-cause: HTML5 print mode unconditionally inherits PDF format footer semantics for page margin boxes. Because default/effective PDF format contains `%{page}`, the generated CSS includes `counter(page)` and renders page numbers even in no-TOC songbooks.

tasks.task: Add explicit HTML5 print config switch to disable page counters independent of TOC (e.g., `html5.paged.page-numbers: false` or equivalent) and thread it into CSS generation.
Implement conditional suppression in FormatGenerator/layout pipeline so default footer page counters are omitted when the new switch is false.
Verify TOC-specific behavior remains intact (`@page toc` suppression and TOC target-counter rendering unaffected).

Alternative implementation path: document and support a config-only override via `pdf.formats.default.footer` with empty page slot for HTML5 print, without code changes; evaluate if sufficient UX-wise.
Add mirrored regression assertions for generated CSS (`counter(page)` present/absent according to switch or format override) in both HTML5 bugfix suites.

test.description: Generate HTML5 print output with page numbers disabled and verify no default footer `counter(page)` appears for song pages.
test.assertions: No `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` rule is emitted when disable switch/override is active.

item.title: Full-Grid-SVG: Taktstriche zwischen Chord- und `|s`-Zeilen driften; `dn~up`-Paare sind optisch zu weit

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/lowlands.cho` and generate HTML5: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Inspect grid blocks containing `|s` lines with connected strums like `dn~up` (e.g. the first grid section).
Compare barline x-positions between chord row and strum row and inspect visual distance of connected `dn~up` arrows.
Observe that barlines are not consistently stacked and connected `dn~up` arrows appear too far apart (not “eng beieinander”).

item.expected-result: In full-grid SVG rendering, barlines in chord and `|s` rows must be vertically aligned at identical x-anchors. Connected `dn~up` pairs should be rendered as tight visual pairs (explicitly tighter than current rendering), matching the requested HTML5 style even if it differs from PDF spacing behavior.

analysis.hypothesis: `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm::grid_block_svg` computes positions row-locally (`my $column = 1;` per row and `x = (column - 0.5) * cell_width`). When strum rows expand tokens via `~` (e.g., `dn~up`), column progression diverges from chord rows and barline anchors drift between rows.

Connected `dn~up` rendering uses full-cell centers for both arrows and only adds a midline connector (`last_arrow_x + 2.8` to `x - 2.8`), so pair distance is dominated by full cell width and appears too wide for the requested “eng” style.

The current unified full-grid SVG path in HTML5 (`render_grid_block_svg` -> `grid_block_svg`) does not maintain a shared canonical beat/bar anchor model across rows; it relies on per-row token expansion, which is fragile for mixed chord/strum density.
analysis.root-cause: The full-grid SVG renderer lacks a shared row-independent geometry contract for beat/bar anchors and uses row-local token expansion, causing cross-row bar drift; additionally, connected strum pairs are spaced by full cell centers instead of compact pair geometry.

tasks.task: Introduce canonical shared x-anchors for bars/beats across all rows in `grid_block_svg`, independent of row-local token expansion.
Map strum `~`-connected pairs (`dn~up`, `up~dn`) to compact intra-beat pair geometry so arrows are visually tight.
Keep existing non-connected strum and bar/repeat semantics stable while applying compact pair spacing only to explicit connected pairs.
Add mirrored regression checks for (a) barline cross-row alignment and (b) bounded connector/pair spacing for connected `dn~up` segments.
Run focused HTML5 grid/strum suites and verify no regressions in standalone strum sections and previous full-grid fixes.

item.title: Refactor Strum SVG rendering and delegate logic to align with renewed Strum-requirement.md
item.justification:
The current strum implementation evolved organically through items 55–61 (SVG migration, bar anchors, token normalization). The renewed Strum-requirement.md (March 2026) introduces several new structural requirements that the current code does not address:
1. **Rest semantics:** `.` in strum lines must mean rhythmic rest (not chord repeat). Current strum_symbol_info() returns an empty-direction hash for `.` with no explicit rest flag, and the SVG renderers do not draw musical rest symbols. The requirement specifies Unicode rest glyphs (U+1D13D–1D13F) scaled by beat duration.
2. **Tilde sub-beat rest rendering:** `~Am` → `/Am` and `Am~` → `Am/` semantics require rendering rest glyphs adjacent to sub-beat chords. Current `_strum_cells_from_text()` and `_normalize_grid_chord_parts()` handle `~` as connectors/pauses but do not produce `/` rest output or Unicode rest glyphs.
3. **Named standalone strum patterns:** `{start_of_strum: <time-sig> <label>}` with `{strum: <label>}` reference is not yet supported. Current parser accepts `{start_of_strum}` as a flex section but does not extract time-signature or label from the header, and no strum-pattern registry exists in Song.pm.
4. **Strum/chord count validation:** Requirement mandates a parsing error when `|s` line entry count doesn't match chord line slot count. Current parser does not validate count parity.
5. **Symbol placeholders:** Current SVG arrows are programmatic triangles/lines. Requirement acknowledges arrows are placeholders pending a dedicated design phase — the code should be structured to make symbol swapping easy (centralized glyph factory).
6. **Three parallel SVG generators** (`strumline_svg`, `grid_block_svg`, `strumline_svg_from_text`) share duplicated drawing primitives (bar drawing, arrow drawing, decoration drawing) without a shared utility layer. This makes requirement alignment changes fragile and high-effort.
This refactoring restructures the SVG rendering pipeline into a shared drawing-primitive layer, adds the missing requirement-mandated features (rest glyphs, tilde rests, named patterns, count validation), and prepares the symbol architecture for the planned design-phase symbol swap.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: `.` in strum lines renders as a visible rhythmic rest symbol (Unicode musical rest glyph appropriate to time context), distinct from `.` chord-repeat in grid chord lines.
Tilde sub-beat rests (`~Am` → rest+chord, `Am~` → chord+rest) render the rest position with a `/`-style rest glyph in SVG output.
`{start_of_strum: 4/4 verse}` extracts time-signature and label; `{strum: verse}` references and re-renders the named pattern at the insertion point.
When `|s` line entry count mismatches the chord line slot count, parsing emits a diagnostic error and rejects the input.
All SVG strum drawing primitives (bars, arrows, decorations, rest glyphs) are consolidated into a single shared drawing-utility layer used by all three SVG paths.
Existing strum rendering behavior for all previously-working token families is preserved (regression safety via mirrored test suites).

tasks.task: Extract shared SVG drawing primitives from `strumline_svg()`, `grid_block_svg()`, and `strumline_svg_from_text()` into a private utility layer (`_draw_bar_svg()`, `_draw_arrow_svg()`, `_draw_rest_svg()`, `_draw_decoration_svg()`) within Strum.pm. Keep public API signatures unchanged.

Add explicit `rest` flag and `rest_glyph` field to `strum_symbol_info()` return hash for `.` and empty-direction tokens. Map rest glyphs to Unicode musical rest characters (U+1D13D quarter rest as default; configurable via `gridstrum.symbols.rest`).

Update `_strum_cells_from_text()` and grid strum cell construction to emit explicit `rest` cells for tilde-adjacent empties (`~Am` → rest cell + chord cell; `Am~` → chord cell + rest cell), replacing current `pause` flag with semantic `rest` when the token is a true rhythmic rest.

Implement `_draw_rest_svg()` to render Unicode musical rest glyphs as `<text>` SVG elements at the cell position, using appropriate glyph for the beat context (quarter rest default, eighth for sub-beats).

Extend Song.pm `{start_of_strum}` directive parsing to extract `<time-signature>` and `<label>` from the header string. Store named patterns in a song-level `$song->{strum_patterns}` hash keyed by label.

Add `{strum: <label>}` directive handling in Song.pm that resolves the named pattern from `$song->{strum_patterns}` and emits the stored strum data as a delegate image element at the insertion point. Emit a warning if the label is unknown.

Add chord/strum count validation in Song.pm grid parsing: after parsing a `|s` line, compare its slot count against the preceding chord grid line's slot count. On mismatch, emit a diagnostic via `do_warn()` and skip the strumline.

Refactor SVG renderers (`strumline_svg()`, `grid_block_svg()`) to use the shared drawing utilities from task 62.1, replacing inline sprintf SVG generation. Ensure `rest` cells are rendered via `_draw_rest_svg()`.
Add `gridstrum.symbols.rest` config key to `chordpro.json` (default: empty = built-in glyph). Regenerate `Config/Data.pm` via cfgboot.pl.

Update mirrored regression suites (`t/html5/09_bugfixes.t`, `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t`) with assertions for: (a) rest glyph presence for `.` strum cells, (b) tilde-rest rendering, (c) shared utility output consistency between `strumline_svg` and `grid_block_svg`.

item.title: Grid chord-strum pairs not vertically aligned — strumline column counting treats sub-beats as separate columns

steps-to-reproduce.step: Generate HTML5 output: `perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl --generate=HTML5 input.cho -o output.html`
Inspect the decoded full-grid SVG in a browser. The chord labels (C, A, D) are NOT vertically above their corresponding strum arrows.

item.expected-result: Each chord label in the grid row should be vertically aligned (same x-position) with the strum arrow(s) of the corresponding beat in the strum row. A strum like `dn~up` is ONE BEAT with two sub-beat movements — it should occupy the same single-beat column as the chord above it, with sub-beat arrows rendered within that column using tight-pair spacing.
item.analysis:
ROOT CAUSE: Strums are NOT chords. The code incorrectly treats strum sub-beat tokens the same as chord multi-part tokens in the column-counting logic.
In `grid_block_svg()` (`lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm`), the `$compute_columns` lambda (line 522) and the rendering loop both call `_normalize_grid_chord_parts()` on ALL `chords`-class tokens — regardless of whether the row is a gridline (actual chords) or a strumline (rhythm directions). This function splits `dn~up` into `['dn', 'up']` = 2 columns.
But `dn~up` is ONE BEAT with two sub-beat movements (down then up within a single rhythmic unit). It should occupy exactly 1 column — the same column width as the chord `C` above it. The two sub-beat arrows should be drawn within that single column using tight-pair spacing (which already exists via `tight_pair_step`).
The problem is in two places:
1. **Column counting** (line 522–536): `$compute_columns` always uses `_normalize_grid_chord_parts()` part-count as column count. For strumline rows, a `chords`-class token should count as 1 column (one beat), not N columns for N sub-beat parts.
2. **Rendering loop** (line 598–640): The per-part loop increments `$column` for each sub-beat part in a strumline `chords` token, causing subsequent tokens to shift right. Strumline sub-beat parts should render at positions within the current beat's column allocation without advancing `$column` by more than 1.
The same issue exists in `_gridline_layout()` in HTML5.pm (used for `$grid_columns` computation passed to `grid_block_svg`) — it counts chords-class parts as separate columns regardless of row type.
The tight_pair_step mechanism (line 612) already renders connected sub-beat arrows close together, but the COLUMN accounting still treats them as separate columns, pushing everything after the first beat out of alignment.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: In grid_block_svg output, each chord label x-position matches the x-position of the corresponding strum arrow(s) at the same beat position (within 0.5px tolerance).

Strumline `chords`-class tokens (e.g., `dn~up`) count as 1 column (one beat) in column computation, not N columns for N sub-beat parts. Sub-beat arrows render within the single-beat column using tight-pair spacing.
Gridline `chords`-class tokens (e.g., `C~Am` — actual chord splits) continue to count as N columns (each chord needs its own column).
Multi-row grids with >2 rows (multiple chord/strum row pairs) also align correctly.

item.title: Leading tilde rest semantics not rendered for chord/strum pairs (`~F6`, `~up`) and symbol output diverges from Strum requirement

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use a grid with leading-tilde chord and strum tokens, e.g. `~F6` on chord line and `~up` on `|s` line.

item.expected-result: Leading-tilde notation keeps explicit rest-prefix semantics in rendered output for both chord and strum rows: `~F6` renders as rest-before-chord (e.g. `𝄼F6` or configured equivalent) and `~up` renders as rest-before-upstroke (e.g. `𝄼↑`) within the same beat/sub-beat model. item.analysis:
Code evidence indicates the leading-tilde segment is currently normalized away in shared chord-part handling, which removes explicit rest-prefix visibility:
1) In `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm`, `_normalize_grid_chord_parts()` removes an initial empty split part (`shift @parts` when first part is ''). This was introduced to avoid geometry drift, but it also suppresses explicit rendering of the leading rest side for tokens like `~F6` and `~up`.
2) `Song.pm::decompose_grid()` keeps `~` splits by creating `class="chords"` with empty members (`split(/~/, $_, -1)`), so parser-level information exists; the semantic loss happens later during normalization/rendering.
3) Current strum rendering path is primarily shape-drawn (`_draw_arrow_svg` line/polygon primitives) while requirement text discusses symbol-level output and configurable symbol mapping (`gridstrum.symbols`). This creates a conformance gap between expected symbol semantics and actual visual pipeline.
4) Existing fixes (items 60–63) correctly addressed geometry alignment and beat-column counting, but not full representation fidelity for leading-tilde rest-prefix semantics in both chord and strum paired display.
Root cause hypothesis: one shared normalization rule is doing two jobs (geometry stabilization and semantic normalization). It should preserve leading-empty semantic intent for rendering while still keeping stable beat geometry.

Leading-tilde semantics are preserved without reintroducing cross-row drift or bar misalignment fixed in items 60/63.
Symbol rendering path is requirement-conformant: either via configurable SVG text/glyph mapping or an explicitly documented equivalent that matches the requirement output semantics.

item.title: ABC delegate warns about uninitialized `$backend` in backend-specific option lookup

steps-to-reproduce.step: Run: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Observe warning output from `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/ABC.pm` line 55: `Use of uninitialized value $backend in exists`.

item.expected-result: No Perl warning should be emitted for backend lookup while processing ABC delegate options. Backend-specific option resolution should use a defined backend key or safely skip backend-specialized lookup when unavailable.

analysis.hypothesis: `beo()` uses package variable `$backend` for backend-specialized hash access (`exists($h->{$backend})`), but this variable remains undefined during execution that hits line 55.

Inside `abc2svg()`, code assigns `my $backend = lc $song->{generate};` (lexical variable), which shadows the package variable `my $backend;` declared near the top of the module. As a result, `beo()` does not receive the initialized backend value.
analysis.root-cause: Variable shadowing in `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/ABC.pm`: backend initialization occurs in a local lexical variable instead of the package-level variable consumed by `beo()`. This leaves `beo()` with an undefined backend and triggers warning noise in backend-specific lookup.

tasks.task: Patch `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/ABC.pm` so backend initialization used by `beo()` is not shadowed (assign package-level `$backend` or pass backend explicitly into `beo`).
Harden `beo()` against undefined backend values to avoid warnings in edge paths (e.g., guard `defined $backend` before backend-key checks).
Run focused delegate regression tests to ensure ABC option resolution remains unchanged except for warning removal.
Re-run the reported command and confirm warning-free execution for this path.
